reference_use.conclusion:
The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract, byte-identical to the workspace Contract and Submission. Only GMT.Ch06.main_theorem and its 12 children are reserved in the DAG, so the bare lpf_* names are free.

The child scope (import GMT.Ch06.Submission plus the replayed namespace and opens) gives the contract notions and SimonGMT Ch01 Densities, Ch03 Rectifiable (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt, blowUpMap, CountablyRectifiable, .unique) and Ch06 (NVector, simpleNVector, nVectorPushforward, nVectorPushforward_simple, TestFormOn, GeometricCurrentOn, support). Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold is not in scope, so C¹ pieces are stated as C¹ maps that are antilipschitz on open sets.

Instance checks:
- NVector carries the operator norm over the ContinuousAlternatingMap norm, so ‖simpleNVector v‖² is the Gram determinant and ‖L_#ξ‖ is the area Jacobian.
- volume on Eucl n is measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace, and μHE[n] = volume there.
- μHE[0] = μH[0].

Mathlib provides the fundamental lemma (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero), measurable_fderiv, hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt, Hadamard via Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le, normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent and LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi.

SimonGMT provides Rademacher, Lipschitz image bounds and image measurability (Ch02/Lipschitz). It provides the full Euclidean area formula with fibre sums and its a.e.-measurability (Ch02/AreaDomain: weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn, ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension) and null critical images (Ch02/AreaLipschitz: area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero). It also provides the upper density theorem (Ch01 simon_theorem_3_6), Lusin (Ch01/Lusin), and the C¹-cover-to-rectifiable direction (Ch03/SubmanifoldCover).

SimonGMT does not provide:
- Lemma 1.2 ⇒, Theorem 1.6/1.9 existence, or the rectifiable area formula; these are the new children.
- A packaged C¹ approximation theorem: Whitney machinery exists in Ch02/WhitneyExtension.lean, but that file is not built.

All 11 child statements pass the lexical validator and elaborate in the comparator child scope. The parent assembly from 3 children is kernel-checked with the standard axioms only. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Steps 4–8 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, printed 3.4–3.9), with the cited results of Simon Ch. 2–3 supplied by the siblings. Setting: U ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^Q open; IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ with θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M (so θ ≥ 1 on M by `pos`); T = τ(M,θ,ξ); f locally Lipschitz on U with f(U) ⊆ V; f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T compact for every compact K ⊆ V; L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P,ℝ^Q) Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable with the derivative clause (for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, every weighted approximate tangent space T_x of (M,θ) at x and every v ∈ T_x, t ↦ f(x + tv) has derivative L(x)v at 0); S ∈ Dₙ(V) with S(ω) = ∫_M θ (L_#ξ)(ω∘f) dHⁿ for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). Notation: J(x) := ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖, M₊ := {x ∈ M : J(x) > 0}, ⟨β, ζ⟩ := ζ(β) for a covector β and an n-vector ζ. For x ∈ M write T_x for the weighted approximate tangent space when it exists (unique as θ(x) > 0, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`).

0. (Degenerate dimensions.) If n > P then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^P, so S = 0; if n > Q then every n-covector on ℝ^Q is 0, hence every n-vector on ℝ^Q is 0 and S = 0. In both cases S = τ(∅, 1, 0): IsRectifiableTriple V n ∅ 1 0 holds trivially (∅ ⊆ V, measurable, Hⁿ(∅) = 0 so countably rectifiable, `pos` vacuous, integrable on ∅, every a.e. statement for the zero measure Hⁿ⌞∅ holds), the integer clause is vacuous, and tauAction over ∅ is 0. From now on n ≤ min(P, Q). For n = 0 all steps below hold verbatim (ℝ⁰ is a point, simple 0-vectors are ±simpleNVector ∅ of norm 1).

1. (Measurability, σ-finiteness, a.e. structure.) x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) and J are a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M ((A,w) ↦ A_#w is continuous), so M₊ is Hⁿ-null-measurable. Since θ ≥ 1 and θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞; U is σ-compact, so Hⁿ⌞M (and Hⁿ⌞A for A ⊆ M) is σ-finite. By `orients` and the clause, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M: T_x exists, T_x = span τ(x) for an orthonormal τ(x) with ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x), and L(x)τ_i(x) = d/dt f(x + tτ_i(x))|_{t=0}; call such x regular.

2. (Local Jacobian bound.) For compact K ⊆ U there is Λ_K with J(x) ≤ Λ_Kⁿ for every regular x ∈ M ∩ K: cover K by finitely many balls B_{ρ_l}(z_l) with f Λ_K-Lipschitz on B_{2ρ_l}(z_l) ⊆ U (U open, f locally Lipschitz); for regular x ∈ K the difference quotients of t ↦ f(x + tτ_i) are bounded by Λ_K, so |L(x)τ_i| ≤ Λ_K, and L(x)_#ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector(L(x)τ) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`), whence J(x) ≤ Π_i |L(x)τ_i| ≤ Λ_Kⁿ.

3. (Induced orientation; printed 3.4–3.5.) Let x ∈ M₊ be regular and v := L(x)τ(x). By simple_nvector_algebra (first conjunct), J(x)² = det G(v) > 0, so v is linearly independent and P_x := span v = L(x)(T_x) is an n-plane. Gram–Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis σ of P_x with v = Bσ, B invertible; by simple_nvector_algebra, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector σ and ‖simpleNVector σ‖ = 1, so J(x) = |det B| and η_x := L(x)_#ξ(x)/J(x) = ±simpleNVector σ. Thus η_x is a unit simple n-vector orienting P_x, and L(x)_#ξ(x) = J(x)η_x. On M ∖ M₊, L_#ξ = 0. Hence S(ω) = ∫_{M₊} θ J ⟨ω∘f, η⟩ dHⁿ.

4. (Consequences of the area formula; printed 3.6.) We use the sibling lemma rectifiable_area_formula: for null-measurable A ⊆ M and a.e.-measurable h ≥ 0, the fibre-sum function N_A^h(y) := Σ_{x∈A∩f⁻¹(y)} h(x) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable on ℝ^Q and ∫_A hJ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^Q} N_A^h dHⁿ. We also use that for null-measurable A ⊆ M the image f(A) is Hⁿ-null-measurable (locally_lipschitz_image (ii); Hⁿ⌞A is σ-finite by step 1), so ∫ 1_{f(A)} dHⁿ = Hⁿ(f(A)).
 (a) If E ⊆ ℝ^Q is Hⁿ-null then Hⁿ(M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(E)) = 0: take a Borel Hⁿ-null E′ ⊇ E; A := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(E′) is null-measurable (f is continuous on U ⊇ M); with h = 1, ∫_A J = ∫ #(A ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = 0 since the integrand vanishes off E′; as J > 0 on A, Hⁿ(A) = 0.
 (b) For compact K ⊆ V let K′ := f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T (compact, ⊆ U). With A := M₊ ∩ K′ and h := θ: ∫_K Σ_{x∈M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)} θ(x) dHⁿ(y) ≤ ∫_{M₊∩K′} θ J dHⁿ ≤ Λ_{K′}ⁿ ∫_{M∩K′} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (step 2); with h := 1 and θ ≥ 1, since f(M₊ ∩ K′) is null-measurable and the counting function is ≥ 1 on it, Hⁿ(f(M₊ ∩ K′)) ≤ ∫ #(M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M₊∩K′} J ≤ ∫_{M₊∩K′} θJ < ∞.
 (c) Hⁿ(f(M ∖ M₊)) = 0: with A := M ∖ M₊, h := 1, ∫ #((M∖M₊) ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M∖M₊} J = 0, and the integrand is ≥ 1 on the null-measurable set f(M ∖ M₊). Also Hⁿ(f(M ∖ spt T)) = 0 by the siblings rectifiable_support_null and locally_lipschitz_image (part (i)).

5. (The image Y.) Y := f(M₊) ⊆ f(U) ⊆ V. Y is Hⁿ-null-measurable by locally_lipschitz_image (part (ii); M₊ ⊆ U null-measurable with Hⁿ⌞M₊ σ-finite, step 1). For compact K ⊆ V, Y ∩ K ⊆ f(M₊ ∩ K′) ∪ f(M ∖ spt T), so Hⁿ(Y ∩ K) < ∞ by 4(b),(c).

6. (Source pieces on which f is an injective C¹ immersion; printed “f|M ∩ B_δ(x) is a diffeomorphism onto an embedded C¹ manifold”.) By countably_rectifiable_c1_cover take charts (Φ_j, Ω_j) of M (C¹, Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω_j), with Ω_j replaced by the open set Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(U); Ψ_j := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ is Lipschitz; M_j := (M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j)) ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Φ_i(Ω_i) are disjoint with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j M_j) = 0; u_j := f∘Φ_j is locally Lipschitz on Ω_j. Fix j. By chart_chain_rule, for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M), with x := Φ_j(w): T_x = range DΦ_j(w) and Du_j(w) = L(x)∘DΦ_j(w); moreover (Ψ_j maps Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets) x is regular for a.e. such w. At such w with x ∈ M₊: L(x) is injective on T_x (step 3: the L(x)τ_i are independent) and DΦ_j(w) : ℝⁿ → T_x is bijective, so Du_j(w) is injective. Apply lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces to u_j on Ω_j: C¹ maps G_{j,k}, open O_{j,k} with G_{j,k} antilipschitz on O_{j,k}, disjoint Borel E_{j,k} ⊆ O_{j,k} ∩ Ω_j with u_j = G_{j,k} and Du_j = DG_{j,k} on E_{j,k}, covering a.e. point of injectivity of Du_j. Let W_j ⊆ Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M₊ ∩ M_j) be the (null-measurable) set of w satisfying all the above and lying in ⋃_k E_{j,k}; Lⁿ((Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M₊ ∩ M_j)) ∖ W_j) = 0. Put A_{j,k} := Φ_j(W_j ∩ E_{j,k}). Then:
 (i) the A_{j,k} are pairwise disjoint subsets of M₊ (M_j disjoint in j, E_{j,k} disjoint in k, Φ_j injective) and Hⁿ-null-measurable (locally_lipschitz_image (ii) applied to Φ_j);
 (ii) Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ ⋃_{j,k} A_{j,k}) = 0: M₊ ∩ M_j ∖ ⋃_k A_{j,k} is the Φ_j-image of an Lⁿ-null set (Φ_j Lipschitz), and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j M_j) = 0;
 (iii) for x = Φ_j(w) ∈ A_{j,k}: f(x) = u_j(w) = G_{j,k}(w) and, by uniqueness of Fréchet derivatives, L(x)∘DΦ_j(w) = Du_j(w) = DG_{j,k}(w); hence P_x = L(x)(T_x) = range DG_{j,k}(w);
 (iv) f is injective on A_{j,k} (G_{j,k} injective on O_{j,k}, Φ_j injective on Ω_j), and (f|A_{j,k})⁻¹ = Φ_j ∘ Γ_{j,k} on f(A_{j,k}), where Γ_{j,k} := (G_{j,k}|O_{j,k})⁻¹ is Lipschitz on G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}); so (f|A_{j,k})⁻¹ is continuous.
 Re-index the pairs (j,k) by k ∈ ℕ: pieces A_k, charts (G_k, O_k), inverses Γ_k, and Y_k := f(A_k) ⊆ Y ∩ G_k(O_k) (null-measurable by locally_lipschitz_image (ii)). For x ∈ A_k let w_x := Γ_k(f(x)) be its parameter; then P_x = range DG_k(w_x).

7. (Tangent agreement for every contributing preimage at a.e. image point; parent 5.3.) Apply weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart with (V, M, θ) := (V, Y, 1) (Y ⊆ V null-measurable, 1 > 0, ∫_{Y∩K} 1 < ∞ for compact K ⊆ V by step 5) and the chart (G_k, O_k): there is an Hⁿ-null E_{2,k} such that for y ∈ (Y ∩ G_k(O_k)) ∖ E_{2,k}, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y 1 y (range DG_k(Γ_k(y))). Let Z_k := A_k ∩ f⁻¹(E_{2,k}) (Hⁿ-null by 4(a)), B := (M₊ ∖ ⋃_k A_k) ∪ ⋃_k Z_k ∪ {x ∈ M₊ : x not regular} (Hⁿ-null, ⊆ U) and E := ⋃_k E_{2,k} ∪ f(B) (Hⁿ-null by locally_lipschitz_image (i)). Claim: for y ∈ Y ∖ E there is an n-plane Π_y with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Y 1 y Π_y and P_x = Π_y for every x ∈ f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊. Indeed, such x is not in B (else y ∈ f(B)), so x ∈ A_k ∖ Z_k for a unique k, x is regular, y ∈ Y_k ∖ E_{2,k}, Γ_k(y) = w_x, and P_x = range DG_k(w_x) is a weighted tangent space of (Y,1) at y; by uniqueness (weight 1 ≠ 0) it does not depend on x or k. (Different sheets through the same image point automatically have the same plane.)

8. (Orientation ζ and multiplicity c; printed 3.7–3.8.) Enlarge E by the Hⁿ-null set f(M ∖ spt T) (step 4(c)) and, for a compact exhaustion K_1 ⊆ K_2 ⊆ ⋯ of V, by the sets {y ∈ K_i : Σ_{x∈M₊∩K_i′∩f⁻¹(y)} θ(x) = ∞}, which are Hⁿ-null because this fibre sum is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable (rectifiable_area_formula) with finite integral over K_i (step 4(b)), hence finite Hⁿ-a.e. on K_i; step 7 still holds off E. For y ∈ Y ∖ E put F_y := f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊. Then F_y ⊆ spt T, so F_y ⊆ K_i′ whenever y ∈ K_i, hence Σ_{x∈F_y} θ(x) < ∞; since θ ≥ 1, F_y is finite, and F_y ≠ ∅. By steps 3 and 7 each η_x (x ∈ F_y) is ±simpleNVector σ for an orthonormal basis σ of Π_y. Two unit simple n-vectors orienting the same n-plane differ by a sign (by simple_nvector_algebra: simpleNVector σ′ = det(B′) • simpleNVector σ with |det B′| = 1 for orthonormal bases σ, σ′ of the same plane). Fix a basis β_1,…,β_N of n-covectors on ℝ^Q and define, for a nonzero n-vector ζ₀, s(ζ₀) := sign(ζ₀(β_γ))·ζ₀ with γ the least index such that ζ₀(β_γ) ≠ 0; s is Borel on nonzero n-vectors and s(−ζ₀) = s(ζ₀). Put ζ(y) := s(η_x) for any x ∈ F_y (independent of x), and ζ(y) := 0 for y ∉ Y ∖ E. Then η_x = ε_x ζ(y) with ε_x ∈ {1, −1}, and
 Σ_{x∈F_y} θ(x) η_x = c(y) ζ(y), c(y) := Σ_{x∈F_y} ε_x θ(x) ∈ ℤ, |c(y)| ≤ Σ_{x∈F_y} θ(x).
 Measurability: Y ∖ E ⊆ ⋃_k Y_k; for y ∈ Y_k ∖ E let x_k(y) := (f|A_k)⁻¹(y) (continuous on Y_k, step 6(iv)). η agrees on A_k with a Borel function off an Hⁿ-null set whose f-image is Hⁿ-null, so y ↦ η_{x_k(y)} is Hⁿ-measurable on Y_k; hence ζ = s∘η∘x_k is Hⁿ-measurable on Y_k ∖ E, and so is y ↦ ε_{x_k(y)} = η_{x_k(y)}(β_γ)/ζ(y)(β_γ) (γ = γ(y) as in the definition of s). Then c(y) = Σ_k 1_{Y_k∖E}(y) ε_{x_k(y)} θ(x_k(y)), a pointwise finite sum (distinct k give distinct points of the finite set F_y), is Hⁿ-measurable.

9. (S as an integral over the image; printed 3.6.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(V), K := tsupport ω, K′ := f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T, and h := θ⟨ω∘f, η⟩ on M₊ (0 elsewhere). Since |η_x(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ and, Hⁿ-a.e. on M, f(x) ∈ K implies x ∈ K′ (rectifiable_support_null), |h| J ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ θ J 1_{K′} a.e. on M₊, which is integrable by 4(b). Apply rectifiable_area_formula with A := M₊ to h⁺ and h⁻: both fibre sums are Hⁿ-a.e. measurable with finite integrals (bounded by ‖ω‖_∞∫_{M₊∩K′}θJ), hence a.e. finite and integrable, so their difference is Bochner integrable with integral equal to the difference of the two lintegrals; subtracting:
 S(ω) = ∫_{M₊} θ J ⟨ω∘f, η⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^Q} Σ_{x∈M₊∩f⁻¹(y)} θ(x) ⟨ω(y), η_x⟩ dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{Y∖E} c(y) ⟨ω(y), ζ(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y),
 using that Hⁿ-a.e. y with M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(y) ≠ ∅ lies in Y ∖ E (E is null) and that for y ∈ Y ∖ E the finite sum equals ⟨ω(y), c(y)ζ(y)⟩ (step 8).

10. (The integer multiplicity representation.) Let M′ := {y ∈ Y ∖ E : c(y) ≠ 0}, θ′(y) := |c(y)| and ξ′(y) := sign(c(y)) ζ(y) for y ∈ M′, θ′ := 1 and ξ′ := 0 off M′. By step 9, since c = 0 on (Y ∖ E) ∖ M′ and θ′ξ′ = cζ on M′: S(ω) = ∫_{M′} θ′ ⟨ω, ξ′⟩ dHⁿ = tauAction n M′ θ′ ξ′ ω for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(V).

11. (Verification of IsRectifiableTriple V n M′ θ′ ξ′ and integrality — Lemma 3.9.)
 • subset: M′ ⊆ Y ⊆ f(U) ⊆ V.
 • nullMeasurableSet: Y is null-measurable, E is null and c is Hⁿ-measurable on Y ∖ E (step 8).
 • countablyRectifiable: M′ ⊆ Y ∖ E ⊆ ⋃_k Y_k ⊆ ⋃_k G_k(O_k); each G_k(O_k) is countably n-rectifiable (O_k is a countable union of balls with compact closure in O_k, on each of which G_k is Lipschitz, and a Lipschitz map on a subset of ℝⁿ extends to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q; cf. SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_image_contDiffOn_open`), and countable unions and subsets of countably n-rectifiable sets are countably n-rectifiable (`countablyRectifiable_iUnion`, `CountablyRectifiable.mono`).
 • pos and integrality: θ′(y) = |c(y)| ∈ {1, 2, …} for y ∈ M′.
 • integrableOn: for compact K ⊆ V and y ∈ (Y ∖ E) ∩ K we have F_y ⊆ K′, so ∫_{M′∩K} θ′ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_K Σ_{x∈M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)} θ(x) dHⁿ(y) < ∞ by 4(b); θ′ is measurable.
 • aestronglyMeasurable: ζ and c are Hⁿ-measurable, so ξ′ is; it takes values in the finite-dimensional space of n-vectors.
 • orients: apply weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart with (V, M, θ) := (V, M′, θ′) (hypotheses just verified) and each chart (G_k, O_k): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′ ∩ G_k(O_k), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ y (range DG_k(Γ_k(y))). For y ∈ M′ ∩ Y_k (⊆ Y ∖ E) with x := x_k(y), Γ_k(y) = w_x and range DG_k(w_x) = P_x = Π_y (steps 6(iii), 7). As M′ ⊆ ⋃_k Y_k, for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′ the weighted approximate tangent space of (M′, θ′) at y is Π_y, and ξ′(y) = ±ζ(y) = ±η_x = ±simpleNVector σ with σ an orthonormal basis of Π_y (step 3); take τ := σ, so span τ = Π_y.
 Hence IsRectifiableTriple V n M′ θ′ ξ′, θ′ is ℕ-valued on M′ and S = τ(M′, θ′, ξ′): S is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: Degenerate dimensions n > P or n > Q give S = 0 = τ(∅); otherwise use regular points where T_x = span τ, ξ = ±simpleNVector τ and L τ_i are directional derivatives.
Local Jacobian bound J ≤ Λ_Kⁿ and induced orientation η_x = L_#ξ/J = ±simpleNVector σ (σ ONB of P_x = L(x)T_x) via simple_nvector_algebra (printed 3.4–3.5).
rectifiable_area_formula: preimages in M₊ of null sets are null, local finiteness of fibre sums and of Y = f(M₊), Hⁿ(f(M∖M₊)) = 0; support_null for f(M∖spt T).
Charts of M + chart_chain_rule + lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces: M₊ is a.e. a disjoint union of pieces A_k on which f = G_k∘Γ-chart is an injective C¹ immersion with P_x = range DG_k(w_x).
